newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks climb on FOMC rate hike decision.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks climb on FOMC rate hike decision.

text.p: Mexican stocks swiftly extended earlier gains at mid-afternoon trade on Tuesday in the minutes following the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's decision to raise key U.S. interest rates 25 basis points.
"It's already more than obvious the FOMC move has gone down well, it really is. The market is mixed and I feel it will continue to climb," an excited Mexico City floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 30.99 points, or 0.81 percent, at 3,858.98.
"There's no uncertainty left on that front, it's time to buy a little more," the trader added.
With a little less than two hours' stock trading left in Mexico, the FOMC announced it had decided to raise the U.S. federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
Dealers noted the IPC may not have sufficient volume to break out of resistance at 3,850 points.
Trading volume was still restrained at 45.1 million shares traded.
